lead.event: Bank Indonesia cuts banks' reserve requirement ratio by two percentage points
lead.headline: Bank Indonesia cuts banks' reserve requirement ratio by 2 percentage points
lead.blurb: The phased cut addresses uneven liquidity distribution across banks despite a solid industry. Conventional banks' ratio falls from 9% to 8% on 1 November and 7% on 1 December, while Islamic banks' ratio drops from 7.5% to 6.5% and then 5.5%, releasing around Rp80 trillion in the first stage. BI said the second stage is tied to adjustments to its Macroprudential Liquidity Incentive Policy, which directs incentives to banks lending to strategic sectors. BI also kept its benchmark rate at 5.75% after its October 2026 Board of Governors Meeting.

macro_flows.event: Indonesian rupiah hits a record low amid fiscal-risk warnings
macro_flows.headline: Rupiah hits record low at Rp18,183 per US dollar
macro_flows.blurb: The currency breached Rp18,000/US$ on 28 October, far below the 2026 State Budget assumption of Rp16,500/US$. Economists warned that continued depreciation, high oil prices and SBN yields above the 6.9% budget assumption could widen fiscal risks as the deficit reached Rp319 trillion, or 1.24% of GDP, by September.

earnings_guidance.copy_decision: rewritten: 1 new articles with a new fact: Total debt declined 13% to US$5.6 billion.

earnings_guidance.event: GoTo reports Q3 and nine-month 2026 profits and raises EBITDA targets
earnings_guidance.headline: GOTO reports Rp441 billion Q3 profit, raises 2026 EBITDA target to Rp3.5–3.7 trillion
earnings_guidance.blurb: The Q3 result reversed a Rp255 billion loss a year earlier and marked GoTo’s third consecutive profitable quarter. For the nine months to 30 September, profit attributable to the parent was Rp1.16 trillion, versus a Rp775.55 billion loss a year earlier. GoTo raised its full-year adjusted group EBITDA target from Rp3.2–3.4 trillion to Rp3.5–3.7 trillion.

earnings_guidance.event: BNI reports nine-month 2026 profit growth as shares rebound
earnings_guidance.headline: BBNI reports 6.6% nine-month profit growth as shares rebound
earnings_guidance.blurb: BNI reported nine-month net profit of Rp16.1 trillion, up 6.6% annually, as loans grew 22.2% to Rp992.5 trillion. Shares rebounded to Rp3,240 at the 29 October close from around Rp2,800 in mid-October. Mirae Asset analyst Nafan Aji sees fundamentals supporting a re-rating but flags foreign flows and MSCI policy.

capital_raising_buybacks.event: Amman Mineral begins its share buyback
capital_raising_buybacks.headline: AMMN begins share buyback with Rp48 billion in purchases
capital_raising_buybacks.blurb: Amman Mineral has bought 12.25 million shares under a roughly Rp1 trillion program targeting about 266.84 million shares, or around 0.37% of paid-up capital. The buyback is scheduled to run through 22 January 2027.

capital_raising_buybacks.event: GoTo reports share buybacks and plans to cancel treasury shares
capital_raising_buybacks.headline: GOTO reports Rp985 billion buyback and plans to cancel 32 billion shares
capital_raising_buybacks.blurb: GoTo’s buyback accelerated after the IDX removed the Rp50 minimum share price on 28 September. By 29 October, it had spent Rp985 billion repurchasing 36 billion shares. The approved cancellation is expected within two to three months after regulatory processes are completed and is intended to reduce outstanding shares and raise existing shareholders’ ownership.
